samples.summary: "Google Docs / Word parity" claim is only half-implemented: while bulleted, the heading loses its heading formatting
samples.evidence: The design note added at docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-134 justifies the model change with "Bulleting a heading applies the bullet *to* the heading (Google Docs / Word parity)". But the implementation converts the block to `type: 'list-item'` and keeps the level *inert*: `blockStyleId()` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:99-114) falls through to `'normal'` for `list-item`, and `getBlockLabel`/`blockTypeToStyleId` (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-style-options.ts:106-129) both report "Normal text". So in Google Docs a bulleted Heading 2 still renders and reports as Heading 2, whereas here it silently renders as body text and only "pops back" to a heading when the list is removed — the parity the doc invokes is not what the user sees, and the retained level is invisible state.

samples.summary: Newly-persisted headingLevel on a list-item is dropped by every export path, so the remembered heading does not survive DOCX/PDF/markdown round trips
samples.evidence: The change promotes `headingLevel` on a `list-item` to real, persisted model state (Yorkie attrs + backend `docs-tree`), but no export/import path was updated: docx-exporter.ts:184 passes `block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined`, pdf-exporter.ts:202 filters `b.type === 'heading'`, serialize/markdown.ts:103 switches on type, and view/clipboard.ts writes `li` meta. A document exported to DOCX/markdown and re-imported loses the memory, so the same bullet un-bullets to a paragraph in one copy and to a Heading 2 in another. The design note asserts the level "round-trips ... like any other block attribute", which is true only for the native Yorkie path.

samples.summary: No way to clear the remembered heading level without also dropping the bullet; the style dropdown mislabels a bulleted heading
samples.evidence: For a bulleted heading the toolbar shows "Normal text" (text-style-group.tsx:86 via getBlockLabel, which gates on `type === 'heading'`), yet the block is remembered as a Heading 2. Choosing "Normal text" calls `setBlockType('paragraph')` (text-style-group.tsx:75 → editor.ts:2802), which clears the level but also removes the bullet — there is no user-visible action that keeps the list and forgets the heading. The design note only says "An explicit 'Normal text' / paragraph command still clears the level", without acknowledging it also destroys the list item.

samples.summary: Overloading `headingLevel` as hidden memory weakens a model invariant; a heading carrying list attrs (the actual Word/GDocs model) or a distinct field would be cleaner
samples.evidence: `Block.headingLevel` previously implied `type === 'heading'`; the change makes it a dual-purpose field whose meaning depends on `type`, and the comment at types.ts:54-61 has to enumerate every reader that must keep gating on `type === 'heading'` for correctness. The alternative that actually matches the cited Word/GDocs data model is a `heading` block that carries `listKind`/`listLevel`, or an explicit `restoreType`/`unlistedFrom` field; either keeps the invariant local instead of relying on every present and future reader remembering the gate.

samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` does not check that the block is a list item, so its contract is looser than its name and docs
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType(block)` (types.ts:337-344) returns `{type:'heading'}` for any block with a `headingLevel`, including an actual `heading` block, even though it is documented as "the block type a list item returns to". The test at packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts also exercises it on a hand-mutated block. Guarding on `block.type === 'list-item'` (or naming the parameter's precondition) would keep future callers from using it as a generic "what should this become" helper.

finding.summary: "Google Docs / Word parity" claim is only half-implemented: while bulleted, the heading loses its heading formatting
finding.evidence: The design note added at docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-134 justifies the model change with "Bulleting a heading applies the bullet *to* the heading (Google Docs / Word parity)". But the implementation converts the block to `type: 'list-item'` and keeps the level *inert*: `blockStyleId()` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:99-114) falls through to `'normal'` for `list-item`, and `getBlockLabel`/`blockTypeToStyleId` (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-style-options.ts:106-129) both report "Normal text". So in Google Docs a bulleted Heading 2 still renders and reports as Heading 2, whereas here it silently renders as body text and only "pops back" to a heading when the list is removed — the parity the doc invokes is not what the user sees, and the retained level is invisible state.

verdict.reason: The code behaves as described (blockStyleId → 'normal' for list-item; getBlockLabel/blockTypeToStyleId → "Normal text"), but it is not a design-fit defect. (a) The design note does not overclaim: docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-134 scopes the "Google Docs / Word parity" claim to the model (bullet applied *to* the heading so the level survives the round trip) and, in the same bullet, states "The level is inert while the block is a list item — every reader (DOCX / PDF / markdown export, blockStyleId, the toolbar label and style id, layout) gates on type === 'heading'". It names blockStyleId and the toolbar label as the very readers the reviewer cites, so the behavior is disclosed, not misrepresented; the identical wording is on the model field at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:54-62. (b) The originating issue spec explicitly makes this a Non-goal: docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:49-52 — "How a list item is *styled* while it is a list item (blockStyleId maps list-item → normal; the issue calls this working as intended)" — and the Approach (:18-32) states the retained level is "inert until the list is removed". The acceptance target is the unlist restore, which is implemented via the shared unlistedBlockType helper across all five exits (document.ts:267,304; editor.ts:2870; text-editor.ts:2169; text-box-editor.ts:1125). Under the design-fit rubric this finding neither fails an acceptance criterion nor exceeds a Non-Goal; it asks for behavior the issue explicitly excluded. Any residual desire for while-bulleted heading styling is a follow-up feature request (minor/non-blocking), not a blocking fit violation.

finding.summary: Newly-persisted headingLevel on a list-item is dropped by every export path, so the remembered heading does not survive DOCX/PDF/markdown round trips
finding.evidence: The change promotes `headingLevel` on a `list-item` to real, persisted model state (Yorkie attrs + backend `docs-tree`), but no export/import path was updated: docx-exporter.ts:184 passes `block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined`, pdf-exporter.ts:202 filters `b.type === 'heading'`, serialize/markdown.ts:103 switches on type, and view/clipboard.ts writes `li` meta. A document exported to DOCX/markdown and re-imported loses the memory, so the same bullet un-bullets to a paragraph in one copy and to a Heading 2 in another. The design note asserts the level "round-trips ... like any other block attribute", which is true only for the native Yorkie path.

verdict.reason: The finding is refuted on two independent grounds. (a) Out-of-scope: the originating task spec lists "DOCX/PPTX export of a bulleted heading's pStyle" under Non-goals (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:58) and its Approach section (lines 22-26) states the retained level is deliberately inert for docx/pdf/markdown export; the canonical design doc records the same decision verbatim (docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-126), and scopes the round-trip claim precisely to "the Yorkie tree node attributes and the backend docs-tree serializer" — so the reviewer's claim that the design note over-claims a general round-trip is factually wrong; the doc explicitly says "every reader (DOCX / PDF / markdown export, blockStyleId, the toolbar label and style id, layout) gates on type === 'heading'". Export output is also unchanged from before the change (the level used to be destroyed at bullet time), so no acceptance criterion of #783 ("un-listing a heading restores the heading") is unmet. (b) Counterexample to "dropped by every export path": the primary internal clipboard path preserves headingLevel on a list-item ungated — text-editor.ts:3404 copies it regardless of block type, serializeClipboard (clipboard.ts:30-36) JSON-encodes the whole block into WAFFLEDOCS_MIME (text-editor.ts:1050/1057), and paste restores it (text-editor.ts:1206, 3578, 3607). serialize/json.ts:49-61 likewise returns the document structurally intact. The reviewer only examined the text/html fallback in clipboard.ts. The residual DOCX/PDF/markdown lossiness is a documented, explicitly non-goal fidelity gap, i.e. at most a minor follow-up, not a blocking design-fit violation.

Choosing "Normal text" calls `setBlockType('paragraph')` (text-style-group.tsx:75 → editor.ts:2802), which clears the level but also removes the bullet — there is no user-visible action that keeps the list and forgets the heading. verdict.reason: The factual mechanics are as described (getBlockLabel gates on type==='heading' at text-style-options.ts:106-114, and setBlockType('paragraph') strips listKind/listLevel plus headingLevel in memory.ts:242-263 / yorkie-doc-store.ts:1371-1415), and I found no single action that clears the level while keeping the bullet (checked clearInlineFormatting editor.ts:2735-2741, ⌥0 text-editor.ts:948-956, mobile Styles menu docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:713-726, docs-context-menu.tsx, indent/outdent editor.ts:2885-2913). However, under the design-fit lens this is not blocking: the change's own spec declares this exact behavior intended ("Explicit 'Normal text' commands ... keep clearing the level — only the list round trip restores", todo:31-32); the "Normal text" label for a bulleted heading falls inside a stated Non-goal (todo:49-52, list-item → normal style id "working as intended"); and design-doc discipline is satisfied in the canonical subsystem doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-134), which explicitly records that the toolbar label gates on type==='heading' and that the paragraph command clears the level. No acceptance criterion requires a "keep bullet, forget heading" affordance, no module is duplicated, and no Non-Goal is exceeded — so the finding is an enhancement/taste preference (minor), not a major fit violation.

finding.summary: Split-propagation of headingLevel onto new list-items contradicts the change's own stated Non-goal
finding.evidence: The branch's plan doc `docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:50-51` lists as a Non-goal: "Splitting a bulleted heading (Enter) — the new item stays a plain list item, as today." The diff does the opposite in three places: `applySplitBlock` now keeps `headingLevel` when `newBlockType === 'list-item'` (block-helpers.ts:256-262), and `yorkie-doc-store.ts:2049-2056` and `:2141-2147` copy `headingLevel` onto split-off list-items. The design doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-176) was updated to describe the new behavior, so the doc set now contradicts the plan's Non-goals rather than the Non-goal being retracted. Either the plan's Non-goal must be revised as part of this change, or the split propagation belongs in a follow-up.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. (1) block-helpers.ts:254-263 deletes `headingLevel` for every split half whose new type is not 'heading' (`if (newBlockType !== 'heading') delete after.headingLevel;`), so a split-off list-item does NOT keep the level; the adjacent `newBlockType !== 'list-item'` branch the reviewer cited only preserves `listKind`/`listLevel`. (2) yorkie-doc-store.ts:2049-2051 copies `headingLevel` only when `newBlockType === 'heading'`; the list-item branch at 2043-2048 copies only list attrs. (3) yorkie-doc-store.ts:2139-2141 is the same `newBlockType === 'heading'` gate. (4) The design doc at docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-177 explicitly states the split deliberately does NOT propagate the level and cites `applySplitBlock` dropping it — matching, not contradicting, the plan's Non-goal at docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:53-57. Retention exists only in `setBlockType` (memory.ts:257-262, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1394/1413/1457-1458), which is the plan's stated Approach. No spec/doc contradiction exists.
